newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dollar key to French stock market future.
newsitem.headline: Dollar key to French stock market future.

text.p: The course of the U.S. dollar will be key to the future of the Paris stock market and as long as the greenback stays above 1.80 German marks French equities can continue to rise, analysts said on Monday.
Wall Street's 3.11 percent fall on Friday, when Paris was closed for the Assumption day holiday, caused sharp selling on Monday morning but analysts said the market still had some upside.
"There has been a lot of adjustment in derivatives positions," said Caroline Menoz at JP Morgan in London.
"But in the cash market there was no panic and the market is cutting its losses. The feeling is that as long as the dollar remains above 1.80 marks it will be all right," she added.
The U.S. dollar's appreciation so far this year, from 4.90 francs on January 2 to a high of 6.35 francs on August 8, has been a major factor in the rise of French shares.
A higher dollar in general boosts the export position of French companies although it also leads to higher raw material costs.
A recent Paribas study showed that 30 percent of the profits of French companies are related to the dollar.
The CAC-40 index rose 36 percent between January 2 and July 31 when the blue-chip index closed at an all-time high of 3,075.67 after touching a intra-day peak of 3,107.31.

Much of this rise was made after the June elections, which brought a coalition of Socialist and Communist Parties to power against the market's wishes but which also ended a long spell of political uncertainty.
The strong dollar helped push the CAC-40 index above the levels analysts were expecting for the end of the year.
At JP Morgan, for instance, the CAC-40 was seen at 3,000 by end-December 1997 and at 3,100 at end 1998, roughly in line with market consensus forecasts.
"A correction had been overdue but now that the market has fallen three percent there could be a basis for a further rise in the next weeks," said another analyst who wished to remain anonymous.
Dollar-related shares, such as Bouygues Offshore, Elf Aquitaine, Total SA and Geophysique were among the top losers on Monday.
Shares that were hurt by the dollar's rise, such as Primagaz, inched higher.
"Today's fall is 100 percent Wall Street. There is no bad news in France today," said Olivier Blitz at IFF.
There are a number of events due to keep investors on their toes this week.
The Federal Open Market Committee(FOMC), which sets U.S. interest rates, will meet on Tuesday and the German Bundesbank is set to meet on Thursday.
The FOMC has a series of recent U.S. data to review to assess the health of the economy and decide whether a rise in interest rates is needed to keep a lid on inflation.

The Bundesbank could be tempted to allow interest rates to go up in a bid to strengthen the mark against the dollar. But economists said that the German economy could well do with the export boost from the weaker mark.
"People are expecting the Fed to do nothing and the Buba to remain unchanged as well," Blitz said.
